Contractor marketing questions, answered straight

The questions home-service contractors actually ask us — about budgets, leads, websites, SEO, and agencies — answered in plain language with no sales fog. Jump to a topic or read it all.

Budget & cost

How much does contractor marketing cost?

Most home-service contractors invest 7–12% of revenue in marketing. In practice that means a one-time website build of roughly $2,000–$8,000, plus $1,000–$5,000+ per month for ongoing SEO, content, and ad management depending on market size and competition. Newer companies typically front-load the website and local SEO foundation before scaling paid ads.

Is it cheaper to buy leads or generate your own?

Buying leads is cheaper to start but more expensive over time. Shared lead services resell the same homeowner to several contractors, so your real cost rises after the jobs you lose. Owned leads from your website and local SEO cost more upfront to build but are exclusive and compound, usually producing a lower cost-per-job within a few months.

What is the highest-ROI marketing investment for a contractor?

For most contractors, the highest-ROI investment is a fast, conversion-focused website paired with local SEO. It captures the high-intent "near me" searches that already exist in your market, works 24/7, and makes every other channel — ads, directories, referrals — convert better. Paid advertising should sit on top of that foundation, not replace it.

Leads & growth

How do contractors get more leads?

Contractors get more leads by ranking in Google's local map pack for "near me" searches, running a fast mobile website with prominent click-to-call, and building steady review velocity that signals trust. The exact mix shifts by trade — emergency trades win on speed-to-contact, while high-ticket trades like solar win on education and follow-up.

What is the best source of contractor leads?

The best source is an owned channel you control: organic local search feeding a website that converts. Unlike purchased leads, organic leads are exclusive to you and get cheaper as your rankings and reviews compound. Referrals are valuable too, but even referred homeowners check your website and reviews before calling.

How do I get leads in the slow season?

Off-season leads come from maintenance plans, planned-replacement marketing, and nurturing past customers by email rather than chasing emergencies. A spring tune-up reminder to last summer's customers, or retargeting homeowners who visited during your busy season, consistently beats cold advertising on cost. Educational content also captures early-stage researchers year-round.

Websites

Do contractors really need a website?

Yes. Even referred and repeat customers check your website and reviews before calling, so a weak or missing site quietly kills work you never see. For high-ticket, trust-driven jobs like roofs, HVAC replacements, and solar, the website is where the homeowner decides whether you look like a professional or a risk.

What makes a contractor website convert?

A converting contractor website loads in under two seconds on mobile, puts a tap-to-call button above the fold, leads with licensing and reviews for trust, and has dedicated service and service-area pages that match what homeowners search. Clear emergency messaging and real project photos turn visitors into calls.

How much should a contractor website cost?

A professional contractor website typically costs $2,000–$8,000 as a one-time build, depending on the number of pages, custom design, and SEO foundation. Cheap $500 template sites usually cost more long-term in lost leads and poor rankings. The right benchmark is return: a site that books even one extra job a month pays for itself quickly.

SEO, ads & timing

SEO or Google Ads — which is better for contractors?

They solve different problems. Google Ads buys instant visibility and works well for emergencies where intent is immediate, but stops the moment you stop paying. SEO takes a few months to build but produces compounding, lower-cost leads over time. Most contractors win by running ads for urgent services while building SEO as the long-term foundation.

How long does contractor SEO take to work?

Local SEO typically shows early movement in 3–4 months and meaningful lead growth by 6–9 months, depending on competition and your starting point. Google Business Profile optimization and reviews often move the map pack fastest, while content and authority for competitive search terms compound over a longer horizon.

What is the most important local SEO factor for contractors?

A complete, active Google Business Profile combined with steady review velocity is the strongest local ranking lever for contractors. Proximity, accurate categories, photos, and a consistent name-address-phone across the web matter too, but a profile earning fresh reviews regularly is what moves you into the top three of the map pack.

Working with an agency

Should contractors hire a marketing agency or do it themselves?

DIY works for the basics — claiming your Google Business Profile, asking for reviews, posting photos. But the website build, technical SEO, and campaign management have a steep learning curve where mistakes cost rankings and leads. A specialist agency makes sense once your time is worth more on the tools and the truck than on the keyboard.

Why hire an agency that only works with contractors?

A trade-focused agency already knows the patterns that win home-service work: storm-response campaigns, emergency call capture, maintenance-plan funnels, and insurance-claim content. A generalist agency relearns your industry on your budget. Specialization means faster results and fewer expensive lessons paid for with your money.

What should I expect from a free marketing audit?

A useful free audit reviews your website speed and conversion, Google Business Profile, local rankings, reviews, and competitor visibility — then tells you exactly what to fix first and why. It should be specific to your business and trade, not a generic report. OnwardCraft delivers a custom audit within two business days.
